artifacts.claimText: Penn's Center for Excellence in Teaching, Learning and Innovation (CETLI) instructs faculty that in all cases they should not upload student work into AI detectors, stating that uploading student work without consent violates FERPA and Penn privacy policies, and noting that AI detectors are not accurate enough to serve as evidence of misconduct due to frequent bias.

artifacts.evidenceSnippetOriginal: In all cases, you should not upload the student’s work into an “AI detector.” Uploading a student’s work without their consent is a violation of FERPA and Penn’s privacy policies. These tools are also not accurate enough to be treated as evidence of misconduct as they exhibit frequent bias.
